passages.title: Ps. 67:1–3
passages.text: Verse 1 adapts the priestly blessing of Num. 6:24–26 . The congregation prays **that** God’s **way** (his **saving power**) **may be known on earth**.

passages.title: Ps. 67:4–5
passages.text: **the nations be glad and sing for joy**. It is likely that the psalmist is praying for the day when God’s rule (**you judge**) is extended to include the Gentiles (see Isa. 2:4 ; 11:3–4 ). The OT looks to a future era in which the Gentiles receive God’s light. This era is brought about by Jesus’ resurrection.

passages.title: Ps. 67:6–7
passages.text: To **fear** God means to hold him and his word in reverence (e.g., 5:7 ; 15:4 ; 25:12 ; see note on 34:8–14 ).

notes.text: **Psalm** . This psalm is a prayer that God will bless Israel with a fruitful harvest (v. 6 ) so that the rest of the world may come to know the true God. Singing this helps Israel to keep its own calling in view: their blessing is not simply for themselves but for the Gentiles too (see Gen. 12:2–3 ).
